evidence: Migration 0137_qoreid_nin_check_once.sql plus its runtime-grants.sql block. WHY: identity-api asked QoreID once per attempt and outside any lock (patient-enrollment.service.ts start(): preflight, then provider.verifyNin; qoreid-verification.service.ts verifyPatientNin: quota, then adapter.verifyNin), so two starts at once, a resubmit after a timeout (QOREID_TIMEOUT_MS 5000, retries 0), a restart after the 24-hour pending enrollment, a retry after a verified answer could not be saved, a retry after 'no record' or a refusal, a profile retry or mismatch, and sign-up then profile (or the reverse) each paid QoreID again (services/identity-api/src/identity/nin-double-charge.spec.ts reproduced all twelve as test.failing on afec3f75). A lock or stored answer shared by every Identity task needs a table. WHAT IT DOES: one table, identity.qoreid_nin_checks (nin_lookup_hmac char(64) primary key, the existing NIN lookup HMAC; state checking|held|answered; attempt_id; question_hmac; outcome record|no_record|rejected|unusable; record_complete; record_source nin_only|profile; answer_ciphertext, AES-256-GCM under Identity's NIN encryption key, never the NIN; key_version; until; created_at; updated_at; CHECKs tie an answer to its outcome, ciphertext and key, a record to its completeness and its source, a record and QoreID's not found to no question, and until to at most 91 days after the row's last change), an index on until, row-level security forced with one owner policy, no grant on the table; five SECURITY DEFINER functions (search_path pg_catalog, pg_temp, owned by the applying role): identity.begin_qoreid_nin_check (system:auth with a correlation id: the stored answer, wait, held, or the lease to call QoreID; insert on conflict do nothing then select for update, one row per NIN, so no lock order and no connection held while QoreID answers; a lease that ended without an outcome becomes a hold until 6 hours after its end), identity.finish_qoreid_nin_check (the lease holder records record/no_record/rejected/unusable, held for up to a day, or released; an answer for a NIN whose patient's login was deleted is not kept), identity.keep_qoreid_nin_record (owner Q110: a live stored record under the caller's key version kept up to 91 days from now, never shortened, its answer, completeness and source unchanged, never for a deleted login's NIN), identity.prune_qoreid_nin_checks (erases rows past until through the until index, never a lease that ended less than 6 hours ago, and the answers for the NINs of patients whose login deletion, 0096, completed in the last day, found from those deletion requests; each limited, skip locked; no row is tested on every tick), and identity.qoreid_nin_check_erased (to no role). EXECUTE on the four commands to hid_identity_runtime and hid_schema_test_runtime only, here and in runtime-grants.sql. PRECONDITIONS (catalog reads, 55000/42501, nothing applied): not already applied; 0127 applied; the seven columns the erasure test reads with their types; auth.accounts has the deleted status; platform.current_actor_subject() md5 cf14c2d4a16d44a79ea9dbef9dc79c2b and platform.current_correlation_id() md5 48d3bf187101d33bfda51dac829aa223 (measured on 0001-0127); the applying role owns identity.patients and identity.patient_identifiers (neither forces row-level security) and may read auth.accounts; identity.patient_account_deletion_requests exists with patient_id uuid, state text and completed_at timestamptz, is owned by a role the applying role uses, and its one owner policy names the applying role (it forces row-level security). Post-checks: owner, forced row-level security with one policy, no table privilege for any other role, SECURITY DEFINER and search_path on every function, EXECUTE only as granted. LOCKS (pg_locks in the applying transaction): ACCESS EXCLUSIVE only on the new table and its two indexes; ACCESS SHARE on auth.accounts, identity.patients and identity.patient_identifiers (reading them to create the SQL function); no foreign key, trigger or change on any existing table. BACKWARD COMPATIBLE: today's identity-api calls none of the new functions; an identity-api image rollback is safe with 0137 left in place (the old image ignores the table). ROLLBACK of the schema: a forward migration may drop the table and functions once no running identity-api calls them. PROVED 2026-11-18 on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16 cluster run as pgrun (fictional data only): UPGRADE 0001-0127 then 0137 by the runner (plan exactly [0137] at the sha256 above), bootstrap and role verification; the file again answers '0137: already applied', without 0127 '0137: 0001-0127 must be applied first', and with another platform.current_correlation_id() body the md5 refusal. The new suite checks the boundary, the system context, argument checks, the lease, holder-only finish, record reuse by every question, an incomplete record taken over by a caller needing a complete one, no-record per question and for the NIN alone, the hold, release, another key version, the table CHECKs, erasure after the login's deletion and the prune; six mutants of the bodies (key version, erasure in begin, holder test, question test, completeness, erasure in prune) each fail it. services/ehr-api scripts/test-staging-schema-upgrade.mjs with HID_REHEARSAL_ADMIN_URL on that cluster (NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS migrator; baseline 128 files with production's runtime-grants.sql): declared [0137], dry run rolled back, applied, migration grants equal runtime-grants.sql (2654 privileges compared), clean install, row security unchanged (208), no-FORCE baseline: passed. services/identity-api/scripts/verify-nin-check-once-runtime.mjs as a login member of hid_identity_api_runtime with three connection pools: no connection held while QoreID answers; two and ten simultaneous checks of one NIN asked once; four different NINs did not wait for each other; a timeout then resubmit asked once and answered 409 NIN_CHECK_IN_PROGRESS; stored rows encrypted and keyed by the lookup HMAC only; 19 audit rows without NIN or HMAC; the prune erased the expired rows and kept live answers. scripts/verify-migration-ledger.mjs (129 migrations) and scripts/verify-platform-graph.mjs pass. release tests: with 0128-0136 absent on this branch alone, the release contract's contiguous-prefix check fails ('missing migration prefix'); with local stubs for the booked 0128-0136 every migration test passes (the remaining failures need infra/cloudflare packages not installed here). REVISED 2026-11-18 after review (the file above is the revised one; production has neither version): a sent check is no longer abandoned at QOREID_TIMEOUT_MS (identity-api keeps reading QoreID's answer up to QOREID_NIN_ANSWER_CEILING_MS, 90 s by default, and keeps it for the retry; no answer by then holds the NIN 6 hours); QoreID's 404 alone is kept as a refusal, other 4xx, 5xx and failures after the request was written hold the NIN 5 minutes, failures that sent nothing are released; a full answer HID cannot use is kept 24 hours as 'unusable'; a record a profile check did not match is kept 24 hours; finish is tried four times; the prune no longer tests every row. RE-PROVED 2026-11-18 on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16 cluster run as pgrun (fictional data only): 0001-0127 by the runner then the revised 0137 (plan [0137] at the sha256 above), bootstrap and role verification; LOCKS unchanged (ACCESS EXCLUSIVE only on the new table and its two indexes; ACCESS SHARE on auth.accounts, identity.patients and identity.patient_identifiers; none on identity.patient_account_deletion_requests, which only the plpgsql prune reads); the revised test/database/qoreid-nin-check-once.integration.sql (adds: unusable kept and reused by every question, a day-long hold, a lease ended 1 s ago held until 6 hours after its end and not pruned, one ended 7 hours ago pruned, the late finish of the lost lease refused, an answer for a deleted login's NIN not kept, the erasure driven by a completed deletion request with a held row of a deleted login's NIN left alone); seven mutants (no lost-lease hold, finish keeps erased answers, a held limit of an hour, no unusable outcome, prune of lost leases, no erasure part, erasure of any state) each fail it; the prune with 200000 stored answers took 25 ms (index scan on until; the erasure joins from the deletion requests to the NIN identifiers and the primary key); services/identity-api/scripts/verify-nin-check-once-runtime.mjs as a login member of hid_identity_api_runtime with three pools passed, now also: no answer then resubmit held 6 hours with a plain message, and an answer slower than the caller's wait kept and reused by another task's retry (one QoreID call). REVISED 2026-11-19 after Ola's review on #276 (three ways one NIN was still paid for twice): the table gains record_source (nin_only when a record came from a check of the NIN alone, a sign-up's or the desk's; profile when a profile check asked with the name and date of birth), set by finish from whether the check had a question; begin answers an incomplete nin_only record from storage to every caller, one needing a complete record too (identity-api refuses it as the first time, 502 QOREID_PROVIDER_RESPONSE_INVALID, without asking QoreID), and takes over only an incomplete profile record; identity-api keeps a NIN-only answer whose record lacks what a sign-up needs but whose name, date of birth and transaction id can be read as that incomplete record for 90 days, not as unusable for 24 hours; QoreID's 404 is kept with no question (it is about the NIN), so it answers every path; and a fifth function, identity.keep_qoreid_nin_record(char, text, integer), lets the desk keep a stored record it matched 90 days from the match (Q110) without taking the row over: never shortened, answer, completeness and source unchanged, only a live record under the caller's key, never a deleted login's NIN, at most 91 days. A profile check's 'no record' stays bound to its question (it may depend on the details sent). Stale text fixed: until is at most 91 days, the sweeper's header says 90 days for a record, and the desk checks through its own NIN-only record check. RE-PROVED 2026-11-19 on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16 cluster (fictional data only): the suite (new cases: the incomplete NIN-only record stored to a sign-up and a profile check, the profile's 404 stored to a sign-up and another question, the keep: 90 days, not shortened by a 1-hour keep, refused for another key, a non-record, a hold, a running check, no row and an erased NIN, argument and context checks, each record's source); four mutants (begin ignoring the source, a keep that shortens, a keep ignoring the key version, finish sourcing every record as nin_only) each fail it; identity-api tsc and 3,283 jest tests, including the three For #276 cases and the keep.
